questions.question: What does a computer virus fundamentally do?
options: Attaches itself to existing files and activates when the infected file is run
Spreads automatically across a network without any user action
Disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users into installing it
Hides at the operating system's kernel level to avoid detection
questions.explanation: Virus ek malicious code hai jo existing files mein attach ho jaata hai — jab infected file run hoti hai, virus execute hota hai aur doosri files ko infect karna shuru karta hai.

questions.question: What is the key characteristic that distinguishes a virus from a worm?
options: A virus can spread entirely on its own across a network
A virus always disguises itself as useful software
A virus requires human action (like sharing a file) to spread further
A virus hides at the kernel level of the OS
questions.explanation: Virus ko spread hone ke liye human help chahiye — infected file kisi ko deni padti hai (email, USB, download). Worm ke uलट, yeh automatic nahi hota.

questions.question: The ILOVEYOU virus (2000) spread through an email attachment. How many computers did it infect within 10 days?
options: 5 million
50 million
5 billion
questions.explanation: ILOVEYOU email attachment 'LOVE-LETTER-FOR-YOU.txt.vbs' ke through millions ne open kiya — 10 din mein 50 million computers infect hue, $10 billion ka damage.

questions.question: Which analogy does the guide use to describe how a virus spreads?
options: Like thousands of bots flooding a server at once
Like a biological flu virus — it needs contact with an infected carrier
Like a postman secretly reading your mail
Like a fake ID card used to gain trust
questions.explanation: Biological virus jaisa — apne aap nahi chalta, kisi infected insaan/file se contact chahiye. Ek infected USB → PC → shared drive → colleagues.

questions.question: You share a USB drive containing an infected file with a colleague, and their computer soon shows the same symptoms as yours. What does this demonstrate?
options: Classic worm behavior — it spread automatically across the network
A supply chain attack through the USB manufacturer
Classic virus behavior — it spreads only when a human action carries the infected file
A rootkit hiding itself from both systems
questions.explanation: Virus ko spread hone ke liye human action chahiye — file share karna jaisa. Yeh worm se alag hai jo bina kisi help ke khud spread hota hai.

questions.question: What makes a worm different from ordinary malware in how it spreads?
options: It requires a user to open an infected file first
It spreads automatically across a network by exploiting vulnerabilities, with no human action needed
It disguises itself as a useful application
It only activates when a specific date is reached
questions.explanation: Worm standalone hai — kisi file se attach nahi hota, koi human action nahi chahiye. Network vulnerabilities exploit karke apne aap spread hota hai.

questions.question: Besides spreading itself, what else can a worm do according to the guide?
options: Carry additional payloads like ransomware or keyloggers and deliver them automatically
Only record keystrokes
Only display unwanted advertisements
Only monitor browsing history
questions.explanation: Worm network bandwidth kha jaata hai aur side payloads bhi carry karta hai — jaise ransomware ya keyloggers automatically deliver karna.

questions.question: WannaCry (2017) used the EternalBlue exploit and needed no user action at all. How many computers did it infect across 150 countries?
options: 3 million+
questions.explanation: WannaCry ne EternalBlue exploit (NSA ka stolen tool) use karke Windows SMB vulnerability attack ki — 300,000+ computers, 150 countries, bina kisi user action ke.

questions.question: Malware spreads from one machine to an entire office network overnight, with no employee clicking on anything or opening any file. What type of malware behavior does this match?
options: A virus — requires a human carrier
Adware — requires a bundled download
A Trojan — requires voluntary installation
A worm — self-spreading via network vulnerabilities
questions.explanation: Bina kisi human action ke poore network mein spread hona worm ki nishaani hai — ek infected machine se poora network infect ho sakta hai.

questions.question: What is the practical impact of a worm on a network's infrastructure?
options: It consumes network bandwidth and can overload servers
It only intercepts keyboard input
It only affects a single file on a single machine
It only displays pop-up advertisements
questions.explanation: Worm network bandwidth kha jaata hai aur servers ko overload kar deta hai — apne aap replicate hote hue.

questions.question: What is a Trojan Horse malware?
options: Malware that hides at the operating system's kernel level
Software that appears legitimate and useful but contains malicious code inside
Malware that spreads automatically without any human action
Malware that only displays unwanted advertisements
questions.explanation: Legit software ki tarah dikhta hai (game, utility, crack) par andar malicious code hota hai — tum khud install karte ho.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the Trojan types mentioned in the guide?
options: Downloader Trojan
Polymorphic Trojan
Backdoor Trojan
Banking Trojan
questions.explanation: Guide mein listed types: Banking Trojans (credentials chori), RATs, Backdoor Trojans, aur Downloader Trojans — 'Polymorphic Trojan' iss list mein nahi hai.

questions.question: The Zeus Trojan (2007–2010) stole banking credentials. How much money did it steal in total?
options: Over $7 billion
Over $700 million
Over $7 million
Over $70 million
questions.explanation: Zeus Trojan ne 70,000+ organizations affect kiye, $70 million+ chura liye including NASA computers — typically ek pirated game ke saath aata tha.

questions.question: Which historical reference inspired the name 'Trojan Horse' malware?
options: A postman secretly opening private letters
A disease spreading through unaware carriers
A guard checking IDs at a building entrance
The Greek mythology story of soldiers hidden inside a gift horse
questions.explanation: Greek mythology ke Trojan Horse jaisa — gift ke andar soldiers chhupe the, waise hi legit-looking software ke andar malicious code chhupa hota hai.

questions.question: You downloaded a cracked version of a paid game from an unofficial website, and weeks later your bank account was accessed without your permission. What likely happened?
options: Your bank's server had a zero-day exploit
A CSRF attack was executed through your browser
A Banking Trojan was bundled with the cracked game
A DDoS attack targeted your bank directly
questions.explanation: Cracked/pirated software ke saath Trojan bundle hona common hai — Zeus Trojan jaisa banking Trojan credentials chura leta hai.

questions.question: What does a rootkit do at a technical level?
options: Spreads automatically through network vulnerabilities
Records every keystroke a user types
Installs itself at the operating system's deepest (kernel) level to hide itself and other malware
Displays unwanted pop-up advertisements
questions.explanation: Rootkit OS ke deepest level (kernel) mein install hota hai aur apne aap ko aur doosre malware ko antivirus se hide karta hai.

questions.question: Why is a rootkit especially dangerous compared to standard malware?
options: It always disguises itself as a game or utility
It always spreads without any human action
Standard antivirus software often cannot detect it because it intercepts system calls and returns fake information
It is limited to displaying advertisements only
questions.explanation: Rootkit OS ke andar se hi system calls intercept karta hai aur fake information return karta hai — remove karna almost impossible ho jaata hai.

questions.question: The Sony BMG CD Rootkit scandal (2005) involved Sony secretly embedding a rootkit in music CDs. How many CDs were affected?
options: 220 million
2.2 million
22 million
questions.explanation: Sony ne music CDs mein rootkit embed kiya DRM ke liye — 22 million CDs affected, bina bataye users ke computers pe install ho jaata tha, massive public outrage.

questions.question: Your antivirus keeps reporting the system as 'clean', but Task Manager doesn't show a process that is clearly consuming resources, and the system behaves suspiciously. What is most likely present?
options: A rootkit hiding itself at the kernel level
A DDoS attack originating from your machine
Ordinary adware
A simple phishing email
questions.explanation: Rootkit ki khaasiyat hi yeh hai ki woh antivirus aur task manager dono se khud ko chhupa leta hai — system calls intercept karke fake info deta hai.

questions.question: What do the two parts of the word 'Rootkit' refer to?
options: 'Root' = a network protocol, 'Kit' = an encryption method
'Root' = highest admin access, 'Kit' = a collection of tools
'Root' = a hacking group, 'Kit' = a malware family
'Root' = the file system, 'Kit' = an antivirus bypass
questions.explanation: 'Root' matlab highest admin access, 'Kit' matlab tools ka collection — isliye rootkit naam pada.

questions.question: What does a keylogger do?
options: Quietly records every keystroke and sends the log to the attacker
Spreads automatically across a network
Encrypts files and demands a ransom
Displays unwanted advertisements automatically
questions.explanation: Background mein quietly tumhare keyboard ke har key press ko record karta hai, phir log file attacker ko bhejta hai — passwords, messages sab caught.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the keylogger types mentioned in the guide?
options: Cloud-based keylogger
Browser-based keylogger
Software keylogger (OS-level hook)
Hardware keylogger (physical device)
questions.explanation: Guide ke types: Software (OS level hook), Hardware (physical device between keyboard and PC), Browser-based (form data intercept) — 'Cloud-based' iss list mein nahi hai.

questions.question: Which defense specifically neutralizes a keylogger's ability to steal a typed password?
options: Using a VPN
Regularly clearing your browser cache
Enabling 2FA, since a stolen password alone becomes useless
Installing a firewall
questions.explanation: 2FA se keylogger useless ho jaata hai passwords ke liye — password chori bhi ho jaaye, dusra factor attacker ke paas nahi hota.

questions.question: Your banking password was compromised despite never clicking any suspicious link, and you recently used a public library computer to check your email. What is a likely cause?
options: A DDoS attack on the bank's servers
A supply chain attack on your bank
A hardware or software keylogger installed on the shared public computer
A CSRF attack from a browser tab
questions.explanation: Public/shared computers pe keylogger install hone ka risk hota hai — physical device ya software hook se keystrokes record ho sakti hain.

questions.question: How does a keylogger differ from spyware in scope, according to the guide?
options: A keylogger is broader than spyware
A keylogger only works on mobile devices
A keylogger only captures keystrokes, while spyware is broader and can capture screenshots, location, and more
They are exactly the same thing with different names
questions.explanation: Keylogger sirf keystrokes capture karta hai, jabki Spyware broader hai — screenshots, file access, location, social media, call logs sab.

questions.question: What does spyware do once installed on a device?
options: Silently monitors activities like browsing history, location, and camera/microphone access, and sends the data to the attacker
Only records keyboard input
Only displays unwanted advertisements
Encrypts files and demands payment
questions.explanation: Background mein chup ke tumhari activities monitor karta hai — browsing history, location, contacts, camera/microphone access, screenshots — data attacker ko remotely bhejta hai.

questions.question: Pegasus Spyware (developed by NSO Group) was notable for what unusual infection method?
options: It spread only through infected USB drives
It required victims to enter their password on a fake page
It required victims to download a fake update
Zero-click exploits — the victim didn't need to click anything at all
questions.explanation: Pegasus iOS aur Android zero-click exploit se install hota tha — tumhe kuch click bhi nahi karna. Journalists, activists, world leaders targeted.

questions.question: A journalist's phone gets compromised without them ever clicking a link, downloading a file, or entering any credentials. What kind of attack does this most closely match?
options: A zero-click spyware attack (like Pegasus)
A brute force attack on their email password
A SQL injection attack
A DDoS attack on their phone carrier
questions.explanation: Zero-click exploits mein victim ko kuch bhi action lene ki zaroorat nahi — Pegasus jaisa spyware bina interaction ke install ho sakta hai.

questions.question: Which of these is within spyware's typical data-collection scope, according to the guide?
options: Only network traffic between two servers
Screenshots, camera/microphone access, and location data
Only firewall log entries
Only DNS lookup records
questions.explanation: Spyware broader scope rakhta hai — screenshots, file access, location, social media, call logs, camera/mic access sab collect kar sakta hai.

questions.question: Who reportedly used Pegasus spyware to monitor the network around journalist Jamal Khashoggi, according to the guide?
options: Saudi Arabia
A US intelligence agency
A private cybercrime group
North Korea
questions.explanation: Guide ke mutabik Saudi Arabia ne Pegasus use kiya journalist Jamal Khashoggi ke network ko monitor karne ke liye.

questions.question: What is the primary behavior of adware?
options: Encrypts files and demands a ransom
Automatically displays unwanted ads such as pop-ups and browser redirects
Hides itself at the kernel level of the OS
Records every keystroke silently
questions.explanation: Adware automatically ads show karta hai — popups, browser redirects, fake alerts. Revenue generate karta hai advertiser ke liye, free software ke saath bundled aata hai.

questions.question: Beyond being annoying, what serious risk can adware pose?
options: It can physically damage computer hardware
It can single-handedly encrypt an entire hard drive
It always installs a rootkit alongside itself
Malvertising (malicious ads) can lead to downloading more serious malware
questions.explanation: Mostly annoying, but some adware spyware ka gateway hai — malvertising (malicious ads) se serious malware download ho sakta hai, browser settings hijack ho sakti hain.

questions.question: After installing a free utility tool, your browser homepage changed on its own and you now see constant pop-up ads. What has most likely happened?
options: A DDoS attack has occurred
Adware was bundled with the free software
A ransomware attack has encrypted your files
SQL injection has affected your browser
questions.explanation: Free software ke saath adware bundled aana common hai — browser hijack, popups, redirects yeh sab adware ki classic symptoms hain.

questions.question: How does adware typically reach a victim's system?
options: Only through physical USB infection
Only through unpatched server vulnerabilities
Only through targeted phishing emails
Bundled together with free software downloads
questions.explanation: Adware free software ke saath bundled aata hai often — user ko pata bhi nahi chalta ki install karte waqt adware bhi saath install ho gaya.

questions.question: Compared to spyware, what is adware's primary purpose?
options: Providing remote access to the attacker
Generating advertising revenue rather than stealing personal data (though it can become a gateway to spyware)
Encrypting files for ransom
Stealing banking credentials directly
questions.explanation: Adware ka primary purpose ad revenue generate karna hai, spyware ka primary purpose data churana — lekin adware kabhi-kabhi spyware ka gateway ban jaata hai.

questions.question: What makes fileless malware difficult for traditional antivirus to detect?
options: It only operates during specific hours of the day
It disguises its file name to look like a system file
It only targets mobile devices, which antivirus can't scan
It runs directly in RAM or abuses legitimate tools like PowerShell, without writing any file to disk
questions.explanation: Disk pe koi file nahi likhta, directly RAM mein run karta hai ya Windows ke legitimate tools (PowerShell, WMI) abuse karta hai — antivirus file scan nahi kar sakta kyunki file hi nahi hai.

questions.question: What is the technique of abusing an operating system's own legitimate tools for an attack called?
options: Credential Stuffing
Living-off-the-Land (LotL)
Supply Chain Compromise
Privilege Escalation
questions.explanation: Living-off-the-land (LotL) attack — PowerShell, cmd, regedit jaise Windows ke apne tools use karta hai, computer restart pe woh gone but damage ho chuka hota hai.

questions.question: During Operation Cobalt Kitty (2017), how long did the fileless malware attack on a Vietnamese bank remain undetected?
options: 6 days
6 years
6 months
6 weeks
questions.explanation: Operation Cobalt Kitty mein PowerShell aur WMI tools use hone ki wajah se attack 6 mahine tak undetected raha — $200M+ theft attempt hua.

questions.question: After a system reboot, security investigators find no malicious file anywhere on disk, yet unusual activity had clearly occurred beforehand. What does this suggest?
options: A fileless malware attack that ran entirely in RAM
A Trojan disguised as a legitimate program
Adware bundled with free software
A standard virus that requires a host file
questions.explanation: Fileless malware disk pe koi trace nahi chhodta — RAM mein run hota hai, restart hote hi gayab ho jaata hai, but tab tak damage ho chuka hota hai.

questions.question: Which legitimate Windows tools are commonly abused in fileless malware attacks?
options: File Explorer only
Task Manager and Control Panel
Notepad and Paint
PowerShell, cmd, and WMI
questions.explanation: PowerShell, cmd, regedit — Windows ke apne legitimate tools use karta hai fileless malware, isliye detect karna mushkil hota hai.

questions.question: What can an attacker do once a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) is installed on a victim's PC?
options: Only encrypt files for ransom
Remotely control the mouse, keyboard, camera, microphone, and files, all without the victim's knowledge
Only display unwanted advertisements
Only monitor network bandwidth usage
questions.explanation: Attacker tumhara poora computer remotely control kar sakta hai — mouse, keyboard, camera, microphone, files, install software — TeamViewer jaisa but bina tumhari knowledge ke.

questions.question: Which of the following is something a RAT-infected computer can be used for, according to the guide?
options: Being added to a botnet
Only serving as a VPN exit node
Only mining cryptocurrency
Only sending spam SMS messages
questions.explanation: Attacker screen dekh sakta hai live, camera on kar sakta hai, files copy/delete, keylog, bank transfers, screenshot, aur tumhare PC ko botnet mein add kar sakta hai.

questions.question: The Blackshades RAT (2012–2014) was created by a 17-year-old and sold on the dark web for how much?
questions.explanation: 17-year-old Swedish teen ne banaya, $40 pe dark web pe becha — 700,000 computers compromise huye, FBI ne worldwide sting operation chalayi.

questions.question: Your webcam indicator light turns on randomly when you're not using any camera app, and files seem to move on their own. What is most likely happening?
options: A firmware update is in progress
A Remote Access Trojan (RAT) is giving an attacker control of your device
A routine antivirus scan is running
Your webcam driver is malfunctioning
questions.explanation: Webcam randomly on hona aur files move hona bina apne action ke — RAT ki classic nishaani hai, attacker ke paas full remote control hai.

questions.question: Which legitimate software does a RAT most closely resemble in function, minus the victim's consent?
options: Antivirus software
A password manager
A web browser
Remote desktop tools like TeamViewer
questions.explanation: TeamViewer jaisa, but without your knowledge — attacker legitimate remote-access tool jaisi hi functionality use karta hai bina consent ke.

questions.question: What is Ransomware as a Service (RaaS)?
options: A government program that helps victims recover from ransomware
A cloud service that automatically backs up files to prevent ransomware
A type of antivirus subscription service
A business model where ransomware developers rent out their malware to other attackers on the dark web
questions.explanation: SaaS ki tarah, but evil — ransomware developers apna malware dark web pe 'rent' pe dete hain, koi bhi coding nahi jaanta buy kar sakta hai.

questions.question: In a typical RaaS revenue split, what percentage does the attacker (the person launching the attack) usually keep?
questions.explanation: 70-30 split typically — attacker 70% leta hai ransom ka, developer 30% — support aur control panel bhi milta hai, pure criminal enterprise.

questions.question: The DarkSide RaaS group (behind the Colonial Pipeline attack) reportedly had which unusual feature?
options: A 'code of ethics' that told affiliates not to attack hospitals
A public bug bounty program
Free antivirus for its customers
Government sponsorship from a G7 nation
questions.explanation: DarkSide RaaS ki professional website thi, customer support, even ek 'code of ethics' — hospitals attack mat karo. Pure criminal SaaS business model.

questions.question: Someone with zero programming skills manages to launch a ransomware attack after paying a monthly subscription on the dark web. What business model made this possible?
options: Social Engineering
Ransomware as a Service (RaaS)
Supply Chain Attack
Credential Stuffing
questions.explanation: RaaS is barrier ko hata deta hai — koi bhi coding nahi jaanta hue bhi malware rent karke attack launch kar sakta hai.

questions.question: What does RaaS provide to its 'customers' beyond just the malware itself, according to the guide?
options: Physical hardware for the attack
Government-issued cybersecurity certifications
Support, a control panel, and even ransom negotiation services
Free legal defense if caught
questions.explanation: Support bhi milta hai, control panel, ransom negotiation services — full criminal enterprise jaise organized business model.
